answer: Require each agent to lock a meaningful stake of value before it can transact, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a ferrous gate that only opens for a key with real weight behind it, the stake turns identity from a free label into a costly commitment. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge: it can earn trust only through small, verifiable work over time, while a knoll of established reputation rewards steady contributors. Attackers must pay the stake for every fake, so Sybil floods stop being profitable.
